title: Retail Intelligence Lab — Consolidated Data Warehouse & Mining Report
course: DTU SE425 — Data Warehouse and Data Mining

sections.1_project_overview: End-to-End DWDM analytics pipeline built on real online retail transactions covering CSV ingestion, ETL, Star/Snowflake schemas, OLAP, Apriori/FP-Growth, Decision Tree/Naive Bayes/kNN, RFM K-Means/DBSCAN, Time-Series forecasting, Text Mining, Spatial, and Multimedia mining.

15_unit_6_coverage_matrix.method: Weekly Resampling, Naive/MA/Trend Forecast + Sequential Item Transitions
Retail Domain Synthesis & Educational Trends Analysis

sections.16_conclusions: Real transactional retail data demonstrates strong customer clustering by monetary frequency, distinct product associations among homeware gift items, and clear seasonal trends. Pruned decision trees effectively predict repeat purchase while preventing target leakage.
sections.17_limitations: The dataset lacks natural GPS coordinates (handled safely via explicit spatial coordinate upload), has unrecorded guest checkout demographics, and exhibits significant positive skew in transaction quantities.
